newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong stocks seen breaking more records.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks seen breaking more records.

text.p: Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index is set to continue on its record-breaking course on Tuesday, still buoyed by a rally in property counters, analysts said.
"I think it can rise further. The focus is on the property investors...their NAV (net asset value) could be re-evaluated," said Tony Yung, research director at Tai Fook Securities Co.

The Hang Seng Index hit a record close at 13,239.39 points on Monday, up 122.60 points on the day. Later, the Hang Seng London Reference index of Hong Kong stocks traded in London rose 27.43 points to 13,266.82.
"The opening will be strong led by Wall Street," said Michael Ng, dealing director at Sassoon Securities, adding that the index could rise 100 to 130 points at the start of trade.
The Dow industrials rose 76.03 points to 6,547.79 on Monday.
"It seems that the banking sector had a small rebound yesterday and I think people will be just going back to banking. Property is still very hot," Ng added.
Analysts said turnover was likely to remain heavy. Turnover was HK$10.55 billion on Monday.
